title: Fire colour: straw or orange?
question: Which of these reads as fire at a glance? One is the renderer's current fire tint; the other is a two-constant change I have not shipped.
context_md:
Same burn, same frames, same everything — only `render.rs`'s two fire-tint constants differ.

**Why this is a separate card.** Every burning thing in the world saturates the heat ramp (it tops out 400C above ambient; grass burns at 520C, a flame at 780C), so fire has no gradient and draws one flat colour — and that colour, `FIRE_TINT_HIGH`, is (255, 210, 110), a pale yellow-white. Over green grass it comes out as **straw**, which is a fair description of what you called colour cycling.

The change is `FIRE_TINT_LOW` (180,55,20) → (150,30,12) and `FIRE_TINT_HIGH` (255,210,110) → (255,138,36).

**The catch, and the reason I did not just ship it:** those constants are not fire's alone. They also colour **lava, fresh quench crust, and warm water** — three looks you have already judged. If you like the orange, someone needs to re-check those three before it lands.

I also tried widening the ramp instead (400 → 1000) on the theory that a gradient was what was missing. It made the fire a murky **olive**, because at a low heat ratio the tint blends over the fuel's own green. Reverted, recorded as a dead end.

meta.touches: fire, lava, quench crust, warm water
